title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued a response to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its approach to shaping AI policy and ensuring it aligns with national values. It commits to developing guidelines, improving transparency, and fostering responsible AI use to meet public expectations and maintain trust.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual outlines how it will oversee and regulate the use of AI in exams and qualifications to protect fairness, integrity, and quality. The guidance aims to ensure AI tools are used responsibly by exam boards, schools and learners, and to meet government expectations for transparent, reliable assessment.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report explores how copyright law influences the development of AI, looking at the legal hurdles and possible gains for creators and developers. It recommends ways to protect intellectual property while still enabling responsible use of copyrighted works in AI training and applications.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government outlines its response to the Lords Select Committee's AI report, highlighting a commitment to strengthen regulation, support innovation, and promote safe and responsible AI development. It pledges to enhance the UK's AI leadership while addressing risks such as bias, privacy, and security through coordinated policy action.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the Terms of Reference for a committee that will review artificial intelligence in the context of public standards. It also includes FAQs to explain the committee’s purpose, scope, and methodology.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of artificial intelligence. Their submission outlines recommendations for responsible AI policy and governance frameworks.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explores how artificial intelligence is changing the way medical products are regulated, with a focus on safety, efficacy, and transparency. It explains how the principles from the AI White Paper can be applied to establish clear, consistent rules for developers and regulators in the medical sector.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy sets out how the organisation will use AI to become the most effective, efficient, trusted and influential defence body for its size. It aims to lead the world in AI‑driven defence capabilities and set a high standard for future operations.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to harness AI’s benefits while mitigating its risks. It details strategies for collaboration, governance, and safeguards to ensure AI is used safely and effectively in transport.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report reviews how AI developers are using copyrighted material under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act and tracks their compliance. It summarises the progress made so far, highlights any challenges, and offers recommendations for improving future adherence.
